prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed the subjects Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II, and Theory of Structures, or at least have taken them.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students should have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students should know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students should be able to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.
Ability to work, lead, and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle, and apply technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Respect for human rights and those with disabilities, and willingness to eliminate discriminatory factors based on gender, origin, etc.
The student is expected to know the properties of steel as a construction material.
The student is expected to understand the different structural typologies for the organization of industrial buildings and framed structures.
The student is expected to know how to dimension and verify a metallic structure according to standards, a structural connection.
The student is expected to acquire the ability to design and direct metallic structure works.

syllabus_topics: Types and products of structural steel.
Limit States to be verified in metallic structures.
Design of industrial buildings. Structural system.
Execution, control, and tolerances in metallic structures.
Selection and design of the roof material to be used.
Determination of actions and dimensioning of purlins.
Calculation of the structural system (frames and bracing) using computational software.
teaching_methods: Field visits to works in progress and permanent installations

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in in-person and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Theoretical Exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (1 Individual Assignment + 1 Group Assignment)
Site visit practices (Minimum of 1 Site Visit with Report Submission)

assessment_rules: The Theoretical Exam requires scoring in both theoretical and operational content, with a score greater than zero in each part. The theoretical content of the exam will weigh 30% and operational content (problems) 70%. To pass the course, it is mandatory to independently pass both the Theoretical Exam and the course assignments, and attend the scheduled site visits. The acquisition of knowledge and abilities for the design and calculation of metallic structures in industrial construction will be specifically evaluated.
